biography.plain_text: Bennett S. LeBow is an American investor who led Miami-based Vector Group, the tobacco and real estate company. He built wealth through computer businesses before acquiring cigarette manufacturer Liggett. He served as Vector's chief executive for fifteen years and remained its chairman until Japan Tobacco bought the company in 2024.

long_biography.plain_text:
Investor Bennett LeBow left the Army and founded a company to continue his Pentagon computing work, choosing business over a return to graduate study. He had trained as an electrical engineer at Drexel University and taught computer design while pursuing graduate studies at Princeton. His military assignment had given him practical experience installing early data systems.

His gifts to Drexel helped develop both engineering facilities and the business school that bears his name. A $45 million commitment financed a new home for the business college, bringing together teaching and research previously spread across several buildings. The resulting hall was named for his late wife, Gerri.
